definitions.explanation: An honorific term used when speaking about the listener's company. Used in spoken conversation, especially in job interviews and business meetings.

examples.japanese: {御社|おんしゃ}の{事業|じぎょう}に{興味|きょうみ}があります。
examples.english: I am interested in your company's business.

examples.japanese: {御社|おんしゃ}で{働|はたら}きたいと{思|おも}い、{応募|おうぼ}いたしました。
examples.english: I applied because I would like to work at your company.

examples.japanese: {御社|おんしゃ}の{企業理念|きぎょうりねん}に{共感|きょうかん}し、ぜひ{貢献|こうけん}したいと{考|かんが}えております。
examples.english: I sympathize with your company's corporate philosophy and would very much like to contribute.

notes:
USAGE:
{御社|おんしゃ} is used in SPOKEN contexts (interviews, meetings, phone calls). For WRITTEN contexts (cover letters, emails, formal documents), use {貴社|きしゃ} instead. This distinction is important and frequently tested in Japanese business etiquette.

NOTE: Both words are keigo (honorific language) and should only be used to refer to someone else's company, never your own. To refer to your own company humbly, use {弊社|へいしゃ} (our company, humble).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {御社|おんしゃ}の{事業|じぎょう} (your company's business)
- {御社|おんしゃ}で{働|はたら}く (to work at your company)
- {御社|おんしゃ}に{応募|おうぼ}する (to apply to your company)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {貴社|きしゃ}: your company (written honorific) — used in letters and documents
- {弊社|へいしゃ}: our company (humble) — used when referring to one's own company
